title: Grits, instant, made with water, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Grits are finely ground corn kernels designed for quick preparation. When hot water is added, they form a smooth, slightly creamy porridge without any added fat. The product is often used as a fast breakfast or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grits are made from whole corn, one of the world’s oldest cultivated crops.
Instant grits appeared in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a convenient food for soldiers and travelers.
Corn provides carotenoids that give grits their characteristic yellow hue.
Grits are a staple in traditional Southern dishes such as “shrimp and grits.”
When prepared correctly, grits retain most of the corn’s dietary fiber.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Grits supply slowly digestible energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes grits suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Corn provides iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Grits have a relatively high GI, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium content in flavored mixes
items.content: Some ready‑to‑eat versions contain added salt; choose unsalted varieties if sodium intake is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Combine 1 part grits with 3–4 parts hot water, stir, and let stand for 2–3 minutes. Add fruit, berries, nuts, honey, or spices to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store grits in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. After opening, use within 3–4 months for best quality.
